# Placeholder {#sec-placeholder}

In the calibrated case, a 40-year-old US man who starts eating 28 g of nuts a
day gains 783 days of remaining life expectancy,
averaged over 20,000 Monte Carlo draws. The cohort dose-response curve
comes from a meta-analysis of prospective studies [@aune2016nut]. From the
starting age, the hazard at age $a$ is multiplied by

$$
M(a) = \exp\bigl(\varphi(a)\, c\, [f(B + \Delta) - f(B)]\bigr).
$$ {#eq-multiplier}

| Bracket member | Women, days      | Men, days          |
| :------------- | ---------------: | -----------------: |
| Calibrated     | 731 (525 to 937) | 783 (563 to 1,004) |
| Face value     | 675 (539 to 812) | 723 (578 to 870)   |

: Days of remaining life expectancy gained from eating 28 g of nuts a day from age 40, mean and 80% interval. {#tbl-reference-bracket}
